chunks: Some Jews said to him (peace be upon him): You had not buried your Prophet when you picked up differences about him.
He (peace be upon him) replied to them: We did not differ about him (in his essence/prophethood) but we differed after him (regarding his succession).

Whereas you had not dried up your feet after coming out of the river (Nile) when you began asking your Prophet: 'Make for us a god as they have gods of their own.' Said he: 'Verily you are a people behaving ignorantly.'

key_terms.جَفَّتْ أَرْجُلُكُمْ: Your feet dried up (crossing the river)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the dispute over Prophet Muhammad's succession and the Israelites' dispute over their Prophet?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs a rhetorical contrast to refute the Jews' claim, distinguishing between a dispute over the Prophet's physical remains versus a dispute over his spiritual and political legacy. By citing the Israelites' demand for a tangible idol during the Exodus, he highlights their tendency toward materialism and superficiality, contrasting it with the deeper theological and leadership questions raised by the Muslim community after the Prophet's death. This narration underscores the Shia perspective that the post-Prophetic conflict was rooted in legitimate questions of authority and succession rather than mere disagreement over burial rites.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 317. Some Jews said to Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him: You had not buried your Prophet when you picked up differences about him,
when Amīr al-mu’minīn replied: We did not differ about him but we differed after him (i.e. about his succession);

whereas you had not dried up your feet after coming out of the river (Nile) when you began asking your Prophet: Make you for us a god as they have gods of their own. Said he: ‘Verily you are a people behaving ignorantly.’ (Qur’ān, 7:138) [1]
